questions.q: What changed Benny's approach to learning languages?
a: He became willing to make mistakes while speaking
He found a course that promised fluency in weeks
He moved abroad and avoided other English speakers
He memorized thousands of words before speaking
questions.why: The overview says a multilingual stranger gave him that simple piece of advice.

questions.q: Why is a goal like I want to learn French a problem?
a: It is too vague and overwhelming, so people give up
It focuses too much on speaking instead of grammar
It ignores the cost of classes and materials
It assumes French is easier than other languages
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you should first define what level of fluency you actually need.

questions.q: Where does the book recommend finding native speakers to practice with?
a: In your own city, for example by hosting travelers
Only in the country where the language is spoken
In online courses taught by certified teachers
At language schools that forbid using your native tongue
questions.why: Lesson 2 says moving abroad distracts you and pushes you toward English speakers.

questions.q: What does the book say about spaced repetition?
a: Study the hardest words first and use flashcards rather than lists
Review easy words daily and skip difficult ones
Space lessons a month apart to let memories settle
Repeat each word aloud twenty times in a row
questions.why: Lesson 2 says early words stick best, so start with the difficult ones.

questions.q: Why should grammar wait until you can hold a conversation?
a: Trying to learn rules and words together only causes frustration
Grammar is not part of speaking any language fluently
Native speakers never use formal grammatical rules
Grammar study makes your accent harder to change
questions.why: Lesson 3 compares it to training wheels that must come off in the right order.
